title: Are there supposed to be two RPG Maker sites?

posts.author: datatech451
posts.body: Ok, so, I was Googling stuff trying to find a solution to a problem, when I accidentally clicked on a website called rpgmaker.net, when it's normally rpgmakerweb.com. ...Is it legit? When you search for rpg maker itself it shows both sites (although rpgmakerweb.com is first). And if it is legit, why? Why the need for two sites? If you investigate for yourself, enter the domains at your own risk. Thanks.

posts.author: Ms Littlefish
posts.body: rpgmaker.net was once upon a time an active website. They went offline some time a year-ish ago, and I think they’ve continued to have issues with maintaining their domain (or something along those lines). I don’t know if they’ve come back online?

Click to expand...
this site is the company's website with the official posts.
besides this there are dozens of fansites in multiple languages for a lot of fan-topics around the RPG-Makers.And those other sites are just the remaining ones - many of such sites went offline over the decades when their owners stopped being fans and the payment for the sites.
And whenever a new PC-version of the makers is released, it usually sparks a dozen or so fansites, with perhaps only one or two of them surviving long-term.

posts.author: orochi2k
posts.body:
The biggest RPG Maker website in the world, 66RPG, died in 2010. (You simply cannot compete with the raw user number of China.
)
Then, DIYRPG, once the biggest RPG Maker website in mainland China after the death of 66RPG, survived all the way to 2020 and died too.
What you see of the current RPG Maker ecosystem is merely a shadow of its ancient glory.
RPG Maker has been reduced to making merely small games that cannot be played for a few hundred hours.
Very sad.
We used to be great!
Only NEOLITHIA remains, and it's eternal!
